title: Three running values at once
idea: TOOL: scale up - a loop can carry three or more running values (total, count, and max) in one pass.

exercises.prompt: Can one loop carry THREE running values - a total, a count, and a biggest-so-far?
options: Yes - just update all three each turn
exercises.explanation: There's no limit. Start three running values, update all three each turn, read all three at the end.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

total = 0
count = 0
high = 0
for n in [4, 9, 2]:
    total = total + n
    count = count + 1
    if n > high:
        high = n
print(total, count, high)
exercises.explanation: total = 4+9+2 = 15; count = 3; high tracks the biggest = 9. Three running values, one pass.

exercises.prompt: Each of the three running values can update on a different rule in the same turn.
exercises.explanation: True. total adds the value, count adds one, high updates only if n is bigger. Independent rules, same loop.
Keep n when it is GREATER than high so far. Output: 8.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a loop tracking total, count, and high for [5, 10].
exercises.explanation: Three starts, three updates per turn, one print. Output: 15 2 10.

exercises.prompt: With total, count, and high ready, which report can you NOT make?
options: The exact order items were entered
exercises.explanation: Running values summarise - they don't remember order. For order you'd keep the list itself. Sum, average, and max are all available.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

total = 0
count = 0
high = 0
for n in [7]:
    total = total + n
    count = count + 1
    if n > high:
        high = n
print(total, count, high)
exercises.explanation: One item: total 7, count 1, high 7. A single value fills every tracker at once.

exercises.prompt: Adding a third running value is the same skill as the second - just one more variable to start and update.
exercises.explanation: True. Two or ten, the recipe is identical: initialise before, update inside. Multiple state scales freely.

exercises.prompt: A good habit when juggling three running values:
options: List them and their starting values before writing the loop
Use the same name for all three
exercises.explanation: Naming each running value and its start up front keeps the loop body clear and prevents 'forgot to update one' bugs.

options: A single pass can carry as many running values as the problem needs
Each value needs its own loop
Multiple state is limited to two
exercises.explanation: One walk, several summaries. That's the full power of multiple state variables.
